flags.message: context.distribution_count is 2 and the band is `elevated`, but the docket shows no true relist: the first distribution (Jun 9, for the 6/25/2026 conference) was superseded six days later by a call for a response, and the second (Aug 5, for the 9/28/2026 long conference) is the petition's first real consideration. The frozen band therefore reflects a mooted pre-response distribution rather than a relist trajectory. I anchored on the `elevated` reached rate as the prompt directs and noted the inflation in reasoning.md; flagging so the salience reading of CFR-superseded distributions can be reviewed.

The frozen band is `baseline` (one distribution, no CVSG), but the docket shows the Court called for a response on Jul 27 2026 after the Solicitor General waived. That call-for-response signal is not among the salience features and has no statpack cut, so the scored baseline understates this petition's position; the forecast adjusts up from the band anchor on the predictor's own estimate of the conditional rate.

The provisioned petition's jurisdiction paragraph dates the Alabama Supreme Court decision December 19, 2026. Its procedural narrative and the snapshot instead give December 19, 2025, followed by rehearing denial February 27, 2026. Treated 2026 in that paragraph as an apparent source typo and used December 19, 2025. No outcome material was retrieved.

Context freezes elevated with distribution_count=2, but the June 17 distribution names September 28, 2026 and the September 16 distribution names October 9, 2026: both conferences are future as of September 17. This appears to be preconference rescheduling after a requested response, not an observed postconference relist. Retained the frozen band/count and adjusted the forecast, rather than treating two entries as two completed conferences.

The snapshot records an August 31 opposition and September 10 reply, but the provisioned document manifest contains only petition/QP text fetched July 18, with the petition marked truncated. Retrieved selected opposition pages from its exact official PDF URL; the reply and complete petition appendix were not reviewed. These limitations are reflected in reasoning.md.

The provisioned document set (documents.json, fetched 2026-07-18) carries only the petition and its QP section, while the 2026-09-17 snapshot shows a brief in opposition (Aug 31) and a reply (Sep 10) on the docket after a called-for response. The cell's documents were not refreshed to the snapshot date. In forward mode I fetched both briefs from supremecourt.gov and read them; a predictor that did not would have weighed the petition against no opposition. Also note context.distribution_count=2 counts the pre-CFR distribution plus the post-response redistribution; the petition has not yet been considered at conference, so the true relist count is 0.

The snapshot and document manifest date the petition entry April 13, 2026, but the petition is signed May 26, its PDF filename indicates May 26, and docketing is June 1. April 13 also dates the extension application. This apparent source chronology mismatch was not used to infer untimeliness or filing-to-disposition latency. Forecast proceeds from the supplied one-distribution forward posture; details are in reasoning.md.

No derived questions-presented.txt was provisioned although the nonempty, nontruncated petition contains readable questions under the heading 'Questions to Review' on printed page 1. Recovered the questions directly from petition.txt; no block to prediction. No BIO or appendix text was provisioned, so descriptions of the lower courts' reasoning remain the petitioner's account.

The provisioned manifest marks the 178-page petition bundle truncated. The questions presented, substantive petition, and pertinent appellate passages were available and supported a complete forecast, but the full appendix was not reviewed. No BIO text is provisioned, consistent with the government's recorded waiver; no opposition arguments were invented.

The docket shows a reply brief filed Aug 10, 2026 (Distributed) but record/documents/ carries only the petition, QP and BIO; documents.json lists no reply. Not a defect of the cell contract, but the reply is the filing that answers the BIO's vehicle arguments, and its absence widened my uncertainty on the vehicle discount.

Comparable-petition context in reasoning.md (the Court's recent denials of post-AFPF disclosure challenges) is from training memory: CourtListener docket searches for those SCOTUS dockets returned nothing. It is pre-snapshot public information, not this case's outcome, and it shaped the number modestly downward.

The frozen band `elevated` (sal-v4) rests on distribution_count=2, but the two distributions on this docket are the pre-response distribution (conference of 5/21/2026, overtaken by the 5/12/2026 'Response Requested' entry) and the post-BIO redistribution (conference of 9/28/2026). No relist has occurred. The Court's call for a response is a real signal the band does not read; the counted 'relist' is not. I kept the band anchor (~17% pooled reached rate) treating the two as offsetting, and noted the trade in reasoning.md.

distribution_count is 2, but the second DISTRIBUTED entry (Jul 29 2026, for the 9/28 conference) is the ordinary redistribution after the Court's Jun 15 2026 call for a response pre-empted the Jun 18 conference; the petition has not been relisted after conference consideration. The elevated band and relist-1 cut therefore describe a stronger state than this docket's. Forecast made from the record as provisioned; noted for anyone reading band-conditioned skill on this cell.

Input coverage limitation, not a blocked cell: documents.json marks the petition truncated; supplied text ends within appendix page 50a, although the substantive petition is present. The snapshot records a July 21 reply, but no reply text is provisioned. Forecast uses the petition, complete opposition, available appellate appendix, snapshot and general precedents; reply responses to vehicle objections were not assessed.

Band `elevated` here rests on distribution_count=2, but the first distribution (Conference of 5/1/2026) was superseded by a response request on 4/22/2026 and never reached conference; the petition's first actual consideration is the 9/28/2026 long conference. The docket's real signal is a called-for-response after a government waiver, which the scorer does not read, while the relist it does read is the reschedule-before-consideration artifact the statpack's relist caption already names. Not a defect in the cell; noted so the band-vs-trajectory mismatch is visible when this cell is scored against the elevated reached rate.

distribution_count=2 here reflects a call for response after the respondent's waiver (distributed 4/22 for 5/14; response requested 5/11; redistributed 7/29 for 9/28) rather than a relist. The elevated band and its reached rate pool this trajectory with true relists; I adjusted by judgment and note it for the evaluator.

The provisioned snapshot file is dated 2026-09-17 but its payload's own creation stamp (sJsonCreationDate) is 07/29/2026, and the last entry is the July 29 distribution for the September 28 conference. Either no docket activity (reply brief, amicus) occurred in August-September or the payload was not refreshed; the cell cannot tell which. Forecast written on the assumption that no reply brief was filed.

The frozen 'elevated' band rests on distribution_count 2, but the second distribution followed a call for response after a waiver (the petition was pulled from the May 21 conference), not a relist after consideration. The band anchor therefore overstates the docket signal for this cell; I anchored below the pooled reached rate and said so in reasoning.md.

distribution_count=2 and band=elevated here reflect a May 5 distribution that was superseded by a May 15 call for response, then a July 29 redistribution for the September 28 conference; no conference has yet considered the petition. The band reads as a relist signal but is functionally a call-for-response signal. I anchored on the frozen band as instructed and adjusted down in reasoning.md; noting so the evaluator can weigh the anchor accordingly.

Band semantics note, not a defect: context.json freezes distribution_count=2 / band=elevated, but the first distribution (Conference of 6/11/2026) was superseded by a 'Response Requested' entry on Jun 3 2026 before any conference considered the petition, and the second (Conference of 9/28/2026) is its first real consideration. The dist-v2 count therefore reads a call-for-response redistribution as a relist. If the elevated pool mixes true post-conference relists with CFR redistributions at different grant rates, a cut by how the second distribution arose would sharpen both the anchor and the relist-increment claim. Forecast anchored on the elevated reached rate as instructed.

The petition is marked truncated and its extract ends during appendix page 53a, before the cited dissent discussion at 54a–55a. The main petition and majority liability analysis were available. The July 24 reply and July 8 medical-provider supporting brief appear on the snapshot but their text was not provisioned. The prediction weighs the available petition against the full BIO and does not assume the missing arguments; see reasoning.md.

context.distribution_count is 2, but the first distribution (Apr 22 2026, for the May 14 conference) was superseded by the Court's call for a response on May 8 2026, and the second (Jul 22 2026, for Sep 28) is the first substantive conference. If sal-v4 or the relist cut reads this as one relist, the elevated band and the relist-increment baseline overstate the petition's trajectory. I forecast the relist-increment from a zero-true-relist state.

Interpretation note, not a claimed parser error: context freezes elevated/sal-v4 and distribution_count=2. The snapshot's three literal distribution notices include an April distribution followed by a response request, and August 5/September 2 notices both naming the future September 28 conference, separated by a rescheduling entry. I retained the authoritative count and band but discounted the inference of repeated completed-conference review. No outcome material was retrieved.
